biological.citation: Structural architecture of the human NALCN channelosome (PMID: 34929720)
biological.summary: Cryo-EM structure of the ~1-MDa NALCN channelosome. UNC79 and UNC80 form an intertwined HEAT-repeat superhelix that docks intracellularly onto the NALCN-FAM155A pore subcomplex. Calmodulin co-purifies bound to the NALCN C-terminal domain, and the UNC79-UNC80 assembly contacts the NALCN DI-DII and DII-DIII linkers. Single-channel recordings showed a low open probability for the wild-type complex.

biological.citation: Architecture of the human NALCN channelosome (PMID: 35387979)
biological.summary: UNC79-UNC80 associates with the NALCN-FAM155A subcomplex through the intracellular II-III linker of NALCN. Disrupting the UNC79-UNC80 interface or the II-III linker interaction significantly reduced NALCN currents in HEK293T cells. Cross-linking mass spectrometry identified calmodulin bound to the NALCN C-terminal domain.

biological.citation: Functional expression of CLIFAHDD and IHPRF pathogenic variants of the NALCN channel in neuronal cells (PMID: 31409833)
biological.summary: In NG108-15 neuronal cells, wild-type NALCN current was carried by Na+, blocked by Gd3+, TTX-insensitive, and potentiated by low external Ca2+. It also showed time-dependent inactivation and voltage sensitivity. The IHPRF mutant W1287L gave no current (loss of function). The CLIFAHDD mutants L509S and Y578S gave higher current densities and slower inactivation (gain of function).

biological.citation: Methylation determines the extracellular calcium sensitivity of the leak channel NALCN in hippocampal dentate granule cells (PMID: 31601786)
biological.summary: PRMT7 methylates NALCN at Arg1653 in the C-terminus. Loss of this methylation reduces CaSR/PKC-delta-mediated phosphorylation of Ser1652 and relieves [Ca2+]e-dependent NALCN inhibition. This increases NALCN activity and neuronal excitability. PRMT7-/- dentate granule cells had a depolarized resting membrane potential and hyperexcitability.

biological.citation: TRPC3 and NALCN channels drive pacemaking in substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons (PMID: 34409942)
biological.summary: NALCN and TRPC3 together form the sustained inward currents behind slow depolarization and pacemaking in nigral dopamine neurons. Blocking NALCN abolished pacemaking in both wild-type and TRPC3 KO mice. NALCN current and mRNA/protein were upregulated in TRPC3 KO mice, indicating compensation.

biological.citation: Progesterone and estrogen regulate NALCN expression in human myometrial smooth muscle cells (PMID: 31935111)
biological.summary: In human myometrial smooth muscle cells, estrogen decreased NALCN mRNA 2.3-fold and protein, while progesterone increased mRNA 5.6-fold and restored protein. Progesterone enhanced and estrogen inhibited the NALCN-dependent leak current. Luciferase assays showed that progesterone response elements in the NALCN promoter drive the regulation, whereas the estrogen response element does not.

biological.citation: The transcription factor unc-130/FOXD3/4 contributes to the biphasic calcium response required to optimize avoidance behavior (PMID: 35115609)
biological.summary: In C. elegans, the transcription factor unc-130 (FOXD3/4 ortholog) upregulates expression of nca-2, the NALCN homolog, along with glr-1 and eat-4 in AIB central neurons. This supports the calcium responses needed to optimize avoidance behavior.

biological.citation: The NALCN channel regulates metastasis and nonmalignant cell dissemination (PMID: 36175792)
biological.summary: NALCN loss-of-function mutations were enriched in human gastric and colorectal cancers among 10,022 tumors. Nalcn deletion in mouse tumors, or treatment with gadolinium (a NALCN blocker), increased circulating tumor cells and metastases without changing tumor incidence. Nalcn deletion in non-cancer mice also caused epithelial cell shedding into the blood.

biological.citation: De novo mutations in NALCN cause a syndrome characterized by congenital contractures of the limbs and face, hypotonia, and developmental delay (PMID: 25683120)
biological.summary: Exome sequencing and molecular-inversion-probe screening found 14 de novo missense NALCN mutations clustered in or near the S5/S6 pore segments in CLIFAHDD families. In vitro, the variants nearly abolished expression of wild-type NALCN, suggesting a dominant-negative effect. This contrasts with recessive NALCN mutations elsewhere in the gene, which cause hypotonia and intellectual disability.

biological.citation: Rapid molecular evolution of pain insensitivity in multiple African rodents (PMID: 31147513)
biological.summary: The AITC-insensitive highveld mole-rat overexpresses NALCN in nociceptors, which ablates AITC detection. This identifies NALCN overexpression as a mechanism that shuts down pain signaling.
